evals.prompt: Our Bitrise production build needs AWS deployment access. Design the AWS side: no static keys, constrained claims, 30-minute credentials, least privilege, evidence, and rollback.
assertions: Uses an AWS OIDC provider and IAM role with temporary STS credentials and never creates an IAM user/access key by default
Constrains issuer, audience, provider-supported workspace/app/repository/workflow/environment subject claims and applies least-privilege policy, boundary/session controls, and short duration
Verifies intended allow, cross-identity/environment/action denial, expiry, CloudTrail/target evidence, rollback, and trust/policy drift

evals.prompt: Roll out an SCP that prevents disabling security logging across all member accounts. Explain grants, canary rollout, break-glass, and proof.
assertions: States that SCPs limit maximum permissions and never grant access, and evaluates inherited SCPs with identity/resource policies, boundaries/session policy, and explicit denies
Inventories organization/root/OU/account hierarchy and starts with a test OU/account before progressive production attachment
Previews blast radius and rollback, tests critical-service allows and target denies, monitors CloudTrail, and uses an expiring independently evidenced emergency-exception path

evals.prompt: Use CloudTrail, Config conformance packs, and Security Hub as release evidence. Can we call a passing pack proof of compliance and store copied event payloads centrally?
assertions: Rejects treating Config packs or Security Hub standards/findings as certification or automatic compliance
Preserves separate opaque CloudTrail event, Config evaluation, Security Hub finding, target resource, policy/version, account/region, freshness and limitation references
Minimizes copied sensitive payloads and requires explicit region/event coverage, retention, access, redaction, outage/delay, duplicate, rollback, and fresh-context probes
